_README: The ten Connecticut state parks the guide is proven on before it goes wide.
Hand-written. makeguides.py reads it and writes data/guides/<id>.json for each.
id binds to the record in places.json; deep is the PROPERTY name in CT DEEP's
property layer, which is the boundary of record; at is a coordinate anchor in
case an id ever changes. why says what this park tests that the others do not.
Chosen 2026-10-22 for spread: north-west hills, central ridges, the lower river,
the shoreline, the quiet corner, and the western lakes. Swapping one is cheap.

parks.name: Sleeping Giant State Park
parks.why: The densest blazed network in the state and the park every existing harness already uses. If routing by blaze works anywhere it has to work here.

parks.name: Hammonasset Beach State Park
parks.why: The most visited park in Connecticut, and the dataset had it named after the preserve beside it while its boat launch carried its acreage. Flat, paved, a beach rather than a hike: a guide that only knows trails fails it.

parks.name: Kent Falls State Park
parks.why: Small, steep, one trail, one waterfall. Also carries a second record for the Sloane-Stanley lease, which tests that a guide is about one place.

parks.name: Gillette Castle State Park
parks.why: A building is the destination. Railroad-bed trails, a river, and a castle with its own season and fee separate from the grounds.

parks.name: Devil's Hopyard State Park
parks.why: Falls, a campground, and colour-blazed loops. DEEP spells it without the apostrophe, which tests that names are joined by more than string equality.

parks.name: Talcott Mountain State Park
parks.why: One famous route to one famous tower, on a ridge shared with the Metacomet Trail. Tests a park whose best trail is not the park's own.

parks.name: Macedonia Brook State Park
parks.why: The largest of the ten, real elevation, a long ridge loop and a campground. Tests the viewer at the top of its size range.

parks.name: Chatfield Hollow State Park
parks.why: Many short blazed trails around a pond, caves and a covered bridge. Tests a network where the choice of route matters more than its length.

parks.name: Mashamoquet Brook State Park
parks.why: The quiet corner. Three parks merged into one (Mashamoquet, Wolf Den, Saptree Run), with the Wolf Den as the destination.

parks.name: Squantz Pond State Park
parks.why: Also classed as a boat launch. A lake beach with a shore trail that runs straight into Pootatuck State Forest, which tests where a park ends.
